title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on the Entry into Force of the Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States
full_text_en:
General Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Entry into Force of the Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States

Fa Ban [2012] No. 252

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

The Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States shall enter into force as of July 7, 2012. Please handle extradition cases between China and Mexico in accordance with the provisions of this Treaty.

This notice is hereby given.

Attachment: Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States

July 20, 2012

Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States

The People's Republic of China and the United Mexican States (hereinafter referred to as "the Parties"),

Desiring to promote effective cooperation between the two States in the fight against crime, on the basis of mutual respect for sovereignty and equality and mutual benefit, have decided to conclude this Treaty and have agreed as follows:

Article 1 Obligation to Extradite

Each Party undertakes to extradite to the other Party, upon request, any person who is found in its territory and who is wanted by the requesting Party for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution or imposing or executing a sentence, in accordance with the provisions of this Treaty.

Article 2 Extraditable Offenses

1. Extradition shall be granted only if the act or omission constituting the offense for which extradition is requested is a criminal offense under the laws of both Parties and meets one of the following conditions:
   (a) If the request is for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution, the offense is punishable under the laws of both Parties by imprisonment for a period of at least one year or by a more severe penalty;
   (b) If the request is for the purpose of executing a sentence, the person whose extradition is requested has, at the time of the request, at least six months of the sentence remaining to be served.

2. For the purpose of determining whether an act or omission is a criminal offense under the laws of both Parties in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article, no consideration shall be given to:
   (a) Whether the laws of the Parties place the act or omission within the same category of offense or denominate it by the same terminology;
   (b) Whether the constituent elements of the offense as prescribed by the laws of the Parties differ. The act or omission as presented by the requesting Party shall be considered as a whole.

3. If the request for extradition involves two or more acts or omissions which are criminal offenses under the laws of both Parties, the requested Party may grant extradition for all such acts or omissions provided that at least one of them meets the penalty conditions set forth in paragraph 1 of this Article.

4. Extradition shall also be granted for an attempt to commit or a conspiracy to commit an offense, provided that the conditions set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article are met.

5. The Parties shall not refuse extradition solely on the ground that the offense is also considered to involve fiscal matters.

Article 3 Mandatory Grounds for Refusal

Extradition shall not be granted in any of the following circumstances:
   (a) If the requested Party considers that the offense for which extradition is requested is a political offense, or if the requested Party has granted the person whose extradition is requested the right to asylum;
   (b) If the requested Party has substantial grounds for believing that the request for extradition has been made for the purpose of prosecuting or punishing the person whose extradition is requested on account of that person's race, sex, religion, nationality, or political opinion, or that that person's position in the judicial proceedings would be prejudiced for any of those reasons;
   (c) If the offense for which extradition is requested constitutes only a military offense;
   (d) If the person whose extradition is requested has been exempted from prosecution or punishment under the laws of either Party because of lapse of time, amnesty, or other similar reasons;
   (e) If the requested Party has rendered a final judgment or terminated judicial proceedings against the person whose extradition is requested for the same offense for which extradition is requested;
   (f) If the requesting Party makes the request on the basis of a judgment rendered in absentia and does not guarantee a retrial after extradition;
   (g) If the penalty that may be imposed by the requesting Party conflicts with the fundamental principles of the law of the requested Party. To facilitate the extradition of the person whose extradition is requested, the requested Party may grant extradition provided that it does not violate the fundamental principles of its law. In such case, the Parties may make appropriate arrangements.

Article 4 Discretionary Grounds for Refusal

Extradition may be refused in any of the following circumstances:
   (a) If the requested Party has jurisdiction over the offense for which extradition is requested under its own laws and is conducting a criminal prosecution or preparing to institute criminal proceedings against the person whose extradition is requested for the same offense;
   (b) If the requested Party, after considering the seriousness of the offense and the interests of the requesting Party, considers that, due to the age, health, or other personal circumstances of the person whose extradition is requested, extradition would be incompatible with humanitarian considerations.

Article 5 Extradition of Nationals

1. Either Party shall have the right to refuse the extradition of its own nationals.

2. If extradition is not granted pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article, the requested Party shall, at the request of the requesting Party, submit the case to its competent authorities for the purpose of instituting criminal proceedings within the limits permitted by its law. For this purpose, the requesting Party shall provide the requested Party with the documents and evidence relating to the case.

Article 6 Means of Communication

For the purposes of this Treaty, the Parties shall communicate through diplomatic channels, unless otherwise provided in this Treaty.

Article 7 Extradition Request and Required Documents

1. A request for extradition shall be made in writing and shall include or be accompanied by:
   (a) The name of the requesting authority;
   (b) The name, age, sex, nationality, and any other information that may help to establish the identity and probable location of the person whose extradition is requested, as well as any available description of that person's appearance, photographs, and fingerprints;
   (c) A statement of the facts of the case, including a summary of the acts or omissions constituting the offense and their consequences;
   (d) The text of the legal provisions establishing criminal jurisdiction, conviction, and sentencing for the offense;
   (e) The text of the legal provisions relating to the statute of limitations or the time limit for the execution of a sentence.

2. In addition to the provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article:
   (a) A request for extradition for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution shall also be accompanied by a certified copy of the warrant of arrest issued by the competent authority of the requesting Party;
   (b) A request for extradition for the purpose of executing a sentence shall also be accompanied by a certified copy of the final judgment of the court and a statement indicating the portion of the sentence already served.

3. The request for extradition and the required documents shall be signed or sealed and shall be accompanied by a translation into the language of the requested Party.

Article 8 Additional Information

If the requested Party considers that the information provided in support of the request for extradition is insufficient, it may request that additional information be submitted within 30 days. This period may be extended by 15 days at the request of the requesting Party. If the requesting Party fails to submit the additional information within that period, it shall be deemed to have voluntarily withdrawn the request, but this shall not preclude the requesting Party from making a new request for extradition for the same offense.

Article 9 Provisional Arrest

1. In case of urgency, a Party may request the provisional arrest of the person whose extradition is sought pending receipt of the formal request for extradition. Such request shall be made in writing through the channels specified in Article 6 or through other channels agreed upon by the Parties.

2. The request for provisional arrest shall contain the information listed in Article 7, paragraph 1, and shall indicate that the documents listed in Article 7, paragraph 2 are available and that a formal request for extradition will be submitted.

3. The requested Party shall promptly notify the requesting Party of the result of its decision on the request.

4. If the competent authority of the requested Party does not receive the formal request for extradition within 30 days of the arrest of the person whose extradition is sought, the provisional arrest shall be terminated. This period may be extended by 15 days at the request of the requesting Party.

5. The termination of provisional arrest pursuant to paragraph 4 of this Article shall not prevent the extradition of the person whose extradition is sought if the formal request for extradition is subsequently received.

Article 10 Decision on the Request for Extradition

1. The requested Party shall process the request for extradition in accordance with the procedures provided for by its own law and shall promptly notify the requesting Party of its decision.

2. If the requested Party refuses the request for extradition, in whole or in part, it shall inform the requesting Party of the reasons for the refusal.

Article 11 Surrender of the Person

1. If the requested Party grants extradition, the Parties shall agree on the time, place, and other matters relating to the surrender. At the same time, the requested Party shall inform the requesting Party of the period of time during which the person to be extradited has been in custody prior to surrender.

2. Subject to paragraph 3 of this Article, if the requesting Party does not take custody of the person to be extradited within 15 days of the agreed date of surrender, the requested Party shall immediately release that person and may refuse a new request by the requesting Party for the extradition of that person for the same offense.

3. If a Party cannot surrender or take custody of the person to be extradited within the agreed period due to reasons beyond its control, it shall immediately notify the other Party. The Parties shall again agree on the matters relating to the surrender, and the provisions of paragraph 2 of this Article shall apply.

Article 12 Postponed Surrender and Temporary Surrender

1. If the person whose extradition is sought is being prosecuted or is serving a sentence in the requested Party for an offense other than that for which extradition is requested, the requested Party may, after deciding to grant extradition, postpone the surrender of that person until the conclusion of the proceedings or the completion of the sentence. The requested Party shall notify the requesting Party of the postponement.

2. If the postponement referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article would result in the loss of the right to prosecute under the statute of limitations or would hinder the investigation of the offense for which extradition is requested, the requested Party may, within the limits permitted by its law and under conditions agreed upon by the Parties, temporarily surrender the person whose extradition is sought to the requesting Party.

3. The requesting Party shall keep the person temporarily surrendered in custody and shall return that person to the requested Party immediately after the conclusion of the relevant proceedings.

4. The period of time during which the person is in custody in the territory of the requesting Party for the purposes of temporary surrender shall be considered as time served in the requested Party.

Article 13 Simplified Extradition Procedure

If the person whose extradition is sought informs the competent authority of the requested Party that he or she consents to extradition, the requested Party may take measures permitted by its law to expedite the extradition.

Article 14 Requests for Extradition by Several States

1. If two or more States request the extradition of the same person, the requested Party shall decide to which State that person shall be extradited and shall notify the requesting Party of its decision.

2. In deciding to which State the person shall be extradited, the requested Party shall consider all the circumstances, including but not limited to:
   (a) Whether the requests are made pursuant to a treaty;
   (b) The seriousness of the offenses, where the requests relate to different offenses;
   (c) The time and place of commission of the offenses;
   (d) The nationality and habitual residence of the person whose extradition is sought;
   (e) The respective dates on which the requests were made.

Article 15 Rule of Specialty

1. A person extradited under this Treaty shall not be prosecuted, sentenced, or subjected to any other restriction of personal liberty in the territory of the requesting Party for an offense committed prior to his or her surrender other than that for which extradition was granted, nor shall that person be extradited to a third State, except in the following cases:
   (a) The requested Party has given its prior consent. For this purpose, the requested Party may require the submission of the documents and information referred to in Article 7;
   (b) The person has not left the territory of the requesting Party within 30 days after being free to do so. However, the period during which the person was unable to leave the territory of the requesting Party due to reasons beyond his or her control shall not be counted in this period;
   (c) The person has voluntarily returned to the territory of the requesting Party after leaving it.

2. If the legal classification of the offense for which the person was extradited is changed during the proceedings, that person may be tried and punished provided that the new legal classification of the offense meets the following conditions:
   (a) It is based on the same facts as those set out in the request for extradition and its supporting documents;
   (b) The maximum penalty that may be imposed is the same as or less than the maximum penalty that could have been imposed for the offense for which extradition was granted.

Article 16 Surrender of Property

1. At the request of the requesting Party, the requested Party shall, within the limits permitted by its law, seize proceeds and instrumentalities of the offense and property that may serve as evidence found in its territory, and shall, if extradition is granted, surrender such property to the requesting Party.

2. Where extradition is granted, the property referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article may also be surrendered even if the person whose extradition is sought cannot be extradited due to death, disappearance, or escape.

3. The requested Party may postpone the surrender of the property referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article pending the conclusion of other pending criminal proceedings, or may temporarily surrender the property on condition that it be returned by the requesting Party.

4. The surrender of the property referred to in this Article shall not prejudice the lawful rights of the requested Party or any third party in such property. If such rights exist, the requesting Party shall, at the request of the requested Party, return the surrendered property to the requested Party without compensation as soon as practicable after the conclusion of the proceedings.

Article 17 Transit

1. Where a Party extradites a person from a third State and needs to pass through the territory of the other Party, it shall request the consent of that other Party for transit. Such consent shall not be required if air transport is used and no landing is scheduled in the territory of the other Party.

2. The requested Party shall, subject to its law, grant the request for transit made by the requesting Party.

Article 18 Notification of Results

The requesting Party shall promptly inform the requested Party of the outcome of the criminal proceedings against the extradited person, the execution of a sentence, or the re-extradition of that person to a third State.

Article 19 Expenses

Expenses incurred in the extradition proceedings in the territory of the requested Party shall be borne by the requested Party. Expenses relating to the transportation and transit of the person to be surrendered shall be borne by the requesting Party.

Article 20 Relationship with Other Treaties

This Treaty shall not affect the rights and obligations of the Parties under any other treaty.

Article 21 Settlement of Disputes

Any dispute arising out of the interpretation or implementation of this Treaty shall be settled through diplomatic channels by consultation.

Article 22 Entry into Force, Amendment, and Termination

1. This Treaty is subject to ratification. The instruments of ratification shall be exchanged in Mexico City. This Treaty shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the date of exchange of the instruments of ratification.

2. This Treaty may be amended by mutual consent of the Parties. Upon completion of all necessary domestic procedures for the entry into force of the amendment, a Party shall notify the other Party through diplomatic notes. The amendment shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the date of dispatch of the later notification.

3. Either Party may terminate this Treaty at any time by giving written notification through diplomatic channels. This Treaty shall terminate on the one hundred eightieth day after the date of dispatch of such notification. Termination of this Treaty shall not affect extradition proceedings already initiated prior to its termination.

4. This Treaty shall apply to any request made after its entry into force, even if the relevant offense was committed prior to its entry into force.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned, being duly authorized by their respective Governments, have signed this Treaty.

Done at Beijing on July 11, 2008, in duplicate, in the Chinese, Spanish, and English languages, each text being equally authentic. In case of any divergence of interpretation, the English text shall prevail.

For the People's Republic of China                         For the United Mexican States

Yang Jiechi                                                                             Patricia Espinosa Cantellano

(Minister of Foreign Affairs)                                                        (Minister of Foreign Affairs)
